focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? The gap-risk numbers are benign — composite 43 (MILD) and P(≥1% gap) ~29%, both under the triggers — but a GREEN light means deploy normal size, and there is nothing to deploy into: the scanner boarded zero qualifying setups. On top of that, the U.S.–Iran war, a constrained Strait of Hormuz with Brent near $90, and Wednesday’s FOMC minutes plus a wall of retail earnings keep an open-ended tail alive. The honest stance is YELLOW by default: no new credit spreads today, keep cash, and re-run the scan tomorrow pre-open when the calendar refills.

U.S.–Iran ceasefire expiring today — the interim ceasefire is set to formally expire, with Hormuz talks deadlocked and Israel striking Lebanon over the weekend, killing a senior Hezbollah commander. Any re-escalation sends crude and the whole tape gapping — the open-ended tail.

earnings.intro: The Q2 reporting season is in its final stretch and this is retail week — Home Depot (Tue), Target/TJX/Lowe’s (Wed), and Walmart (Thu) headline, with July inflation data already cleared. Because the scan boarded zero setups today there is nothing to keep clear of, but any future spread must expire before its name’s print. Watch the FOMC minutes Wednesday as the macro overlay.

rows.why: First of the retail wall — a read on big-ticket spending and professional contractor demand. Consensus has been revised lower and HD missed revenue last quarter, so a guidance stumble gaps it. First consumer signal of the week.
rows.angle: Don’t hold an HD spread through Tuesday. A clean beat-and-gap can set up a Type A later in the week.

rows.why: Target has been a serial gapper and is down ~40% over five years — discretionary spending, foot traffic, and digital sales are the swing factors. TJX (off-price) and Lowe’s (home renovation) report the same day, and FOMC minutes hit at 2pm. Stacked single-stock and macro risk.
rows.angle: Do not carry a Target spread through Wednesday. A miss-and-gap-down becomes a Type A bear-call setup next session.

rows.why: The week’s marquee print — a read on lower-income spending and grocery inflation. Walmart has lost momentum this year after years of outperformance; in-line results with cautious guidance could still move it. Deere also reports Thursday.
rows.angle: Keep any retail spread to a DTE that clears its earnings date. Watch WMT’s consumer commentary for the whole tape’s tone.
